old_title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal identify Vini Jr alternatives, Liverpool in defender deal
new_title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal identify Vinicius Jr alternatives as Romero eyes switch
old_text:
Arsenal have moved on from their chase of Vinicius Jr after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid and the Gunners have now reignited their interest in Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez while PSG's Bradley Barcola is also on their list.
But Bruno Guimaraes has finally officially completed his £75m move from Newcastle United with the deal for the 28-year-old midfielder representing a key piece of business of Mikel Arteta ahead of Arsenal's title defence.
Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca - though an initial offer of £38m has been rejected.
Liverpool, meanwhile, also want to sign Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and have lined up his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye in what could be a double swoop for Andoni Iraola's side. The European champions may be willing to let them go, especially following Maghnes Akliouche signing from Monaco, while the Reds also look to have secured much-needed defender help with ex-Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo set for a loan deal, with an option to buy, at Anfield.
Elsewhere, Manchester United have added to their ranks by bringing in a teenage midfielder and they are exploring their options at left-back with Lewis Hall reportedly now set on a move to Old Trafford, but Newcastle are determined to stop the exodus and insist he is not for sale.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below:

Mohamed Salah will be something of an incongruous sight at Trabzonspor - a stark drop in prestige from Liverpool - but the move to football's growing, lucrative retirement home does offer intrigue, Richard Jolly writes:
Newcastle consider experienced Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg to bolster midfield
A number of reports this weekend have linked Newcastle with a move for Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. The former Southampton and Tottenham man possesses prior Premier League experience and, while not a direct replacement for Bruno Guimaraes or Sandro Tonali, could bolster an area now of need.
Manchester United told Lewis Hall not for sale
According to Sky Sports, Manchester United have been told that Lewis Hall is not for sale by Newcastle as the Tyneside club bid to hold on to at least one key figure this summer. Manchester United are keen to add a versatile left-back option but knew a deal for Hall might be difficult - and it appears he's likely to stay at St James' Park.
WATCH: Bruno Guimaraes bids farewell to Newcastle fans
The manner of his departure while club captain may not necessarily please Newcastle fans, but this is a nice farewell from Bruno Guimaraes as he heads to Arsenal.
Newcastle sporting director admits Bruno Guimaraes wanted to leave
Ross Wilson, Newcastle's sporting director, has revealed that Bruno Guimaraes expressed his desire to leave the club - providing little choice as they granted him a switch to Arsenal.
"What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on," he said.
"That doesn't mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number.
"There's no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer - it wasn't.
"But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen."
Arsenal hold nerve after missing out on Vinicius Jr with three alternative targets
Arsenal intend to hold their nerve and assess alternative options after missing out on Vinicius Jr with the Real Madrid superstar signing a contract extension at the Bernabeu on Thursday.
Mikel Arteta is still eager to bring in a new left winger, though, with three notable options still on the table.
Arsenal made a serious bid to sign Vinicius Jr, with an agreement close on personal terms, but the 26-year-old ultimately opted to commit his future to Madrid in a deal until 2032.
Liverpool on the brink of loan deal for Ronald Araujo
Liverpool are close to agreeing a loan deal for Barcelona's Ronald Araujo to give them much-needed reinforcements in defence.
The Merseyside club are looking to complete a loan with an option to buy the Uruguay international.
The 27-year-old former Barcelona captain is set to become Andoni Iraola's second signing at Anfield, after winger Victor Munoz.
Araujo, primarily a central defender but who can also play right-back, will help give Iraola more strength in depth in both positions.

new_text:
Arsenal have moved on from their chase of Vinicius Jr after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid and the Gunners have now reignited their interest in Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez, while PSG's Bradley Barcola is also on their list.
Meanwhile, Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca - who are considering a second bid after an initial offer of £38m was rejected.
Liverpool, meanwhile, also want to sign Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and have lined up his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye in what could be a double swoop for Andoni Iraola's side, while the Reds also look to have secured much-needed defender help with ex-Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo set for a loan deal with an option to buy.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below
Arsenal outgoings - could Zubimendi be on the move?
With Arsenal splashing £75m on Bruno Guimaraes, Mikel Arteta may be required to sanction some sales.
That has led Mundo Deportivo to report that Martin Zubimendi, who only joined Arsenal last year, could leave the club, but only if a potential suitor matches their £77m asking price.
Meanwhile, West Ham are exploring a move for Reiss Nelson who has entered the final year of his contract, as per Sky Sports.
Another Chelsea-Strasbourg loan on the horizon
Filip Jorgensen is set to move to Strasbourg on loan, according to Sky Sports, becoming the latest Chelsea player to make that jump to the Alsace sister club.
Aston Villa in talks for Palhinha - but face competition from Newcastle?
Aston Villa transfer chief Damian Viadagany has confirmed the club are in talks to sign Joao Palhinha from Bayern Munich.
He told Bild: "We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement.
"If something should happen, it is always on the basis of the great respect we feel for FC Bayern.
"We are friendly clubs; our relationship with Max Eberl (Bayern's director of sport), Christoph Freund (Bayern sporting director) and all other responsible persons is excellent.
"Therefore, I cannot and do not want to comment on any further details."
This comes amid reports that Newcastle are also keen on the Portuguese midfielder, who was on loan at Tottenham last term, joining Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg on the list of potential Bruno Guimaraes replacements.
Palace getting busy
As well as potentially signing Dwight McNeil in a swap deal, Crystal Palace are interested in Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and Torino winger Alieu Njie, according to Sky Sports.
Youssef Chermiti stretchered off amid Galatasaray interest
News emerged before Rangers' clash with Hibernian on Sunday that Galatasaray had seen a bid rejected for striker Youssef Chermiti, with the Gers unwilling to sell.
However, the Turkish side's pursuit of Chermiti may now be over after he was stretchered off in that game.
Man Utd working over deal for EFL Apprentice of the Year
Manchester United are working on a deal to sign Leicester City starlet Louis Page, according to BBC Sport.
Page, an 18-year-old midfielder, was named the EFL Apprentice of the Year last term and is an England U20 international.
Hull announce seventh signing of summer
Sweden wing-back Elliot Stroud has joined Hull from Mjallby for an undisclosed fee on a four-year contract.
Shea Charles set for Fulham medical
Southampton midfielder Shea Charles is set to undergo a medical at Fulham after the clubs agreed a deal worth up to £30m, according to the Press Association.
The 22-year-old is expected to sign a five-year contract at Craven Cottage and become the most expensive Northern Irish footballer.
Fulham will pay an initial fee of £26m, while the transfer includes a further £4m in performance-related add-ons.
Ipswich bid for Exequiel Palacios
Ipswich Town have sent in a bid for Exequiel Palacios, according to Fabrizio Romano.
The Argentinian, who is among their key targets, is also being pursued by four other clubs in the Premier League and Bundesliga.
Another big name set for Turkey move
Mohamed Salah's switch to Trabzonspor may have knocked over the first domino of big names making moves to Turkey this summer.
That's because now, Fenerbahce are set to finalise a deal to sign Belgium striker Romelu Lukaku from Napoli, as per Gazzetta dello Sport.
Chelsea will receive a sell-on fee.
